target_customer: Employers hiring software developers (paid a commission per hire); developers used it free
problem: Resumes are a poor screen for developer ability; employers wanted verified coding skill.
business_model: Recruiting marketplace with employer commission per hire

technical_complexity.rationale: Code execution sandbox, scoring and keystroke replay are moderately hard but well within a two-person team.

defensibility.rationale: TechCrunch notes the idea had been tried before and competitors existed; no network or data moat in two months.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pinterest acquired the team about two months after launch (October 2013) and shut the product down.

market_need_then: Developer hiring demand was high in 2013; TechCrunch (2013-08) describes the pitch as replacing resumes with a score. No quantitative demand data retrieved.

branding.domain_note: Domain hackermeter.com per YC listing; acquisition history not found.
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch headline coverage on launch and acquisition (Aug and Oct 2013).

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive compound name; coverage was about the product and acquisition, not the brand.

outcome_analysis: Hackermeter launched around the Summer 2013 batch and was acquired by Pinterest in October 2013, about two months after launch, primarily as a talent acquisition with the product shut down and the founders joining Pinterest as engineers. Terms were undisclosed and described as not large, so this reads as a soft landing rather than a product outcome.
notes: Batch conflict: YC says Summer 2013; CB Insights and TechCrunch (2013-10) say Winter 2013 (CB Insights via search summary). Funding unverified: Dealroom says 120,000 USD from YC on 2013-08-13, CB Insights says 20K raised, AngelList showed an attempted 750K raise; none recorded as rounds. Deal terms undisclosed. Competitor traction and funding not given in TechCrunch. hackermeter.com not fetched. Web Archive skipped.
